sections.h2: Is a quick sale realistic in Conroe?
sections.html:
Yes. In Conroe the choice is usually a cash contract that funds within weeks or a conventional listing that trades speed for a stronger price.

The city holds the Montgomery County courthouse, with Interstate 45 running alongside. Reasons to sell range widely, from an inherited house to a tenant-occupied rental to a mortgage in trouble.

  • Cash contract: bought as-is, no open houses, and you set the closing day.
  • Listing: more buyers, but also inspections, loan timelines and repair demands.
  • Lease-assigned sale: the buyer takes over an existing tenancy.
  • Pre-auction sale: must fund before the posted auction day.

Conroe is growing quickly. By July 1, 2025 it had an estimated 119,564 residents, up 33.0% from 89,899 in April 2020. The city itself spread from 52.71 square miles in 2010 to 72.00 in 2020, and 82.8% of its people lived at one address all year.

There are 39,852 households averaging 2.52 people. Since the borders keep moving outward, confirm your address is inside the city before telling a buyer what taxes to expect. The average trip to work is 28.6 minutes, a number that matters to anyone commuting toward Houston on the interstate.

This is a big city. Shoppers drawn to the courthouse square, the interstate corridor or Lake Conroe, about seven miles northwest, are rarely the same people. The school district stretches across 330 square miles, so which campus serves a house follows its street address, not a Conroe mailing label. Ask the district about zoning with your exact address in hand.

sections.h2: Montgomery County tax bills and due dates
sections.html:
Statements go out in October and can be paid on receipt. Interest and penalty begin February 1, and a mailed payment is judged by its postmark.

Penalty opens at 6 percent, gains a point every month, and takes a last 2 points on July 1 to finish at 12 percent. Interest of 1 percent a month piles on besides. The office takes partial payments, yet whatever remains after January 31 keeps growing. Phone (936) 539-7897 or visit 400 N. San Jacinto Street.

Disputes over value, exemptions and protests belong to Montgomery Central Appraisal District. Its protest deadline is May 15, or 30 days after your notice arrives if that comes later.

sections.h2: Who pays the bill when a house sells?
sections.html:
The settlement statement tells the story. The tax office suggests that new owners read their closing papers or phone the title company, which may have taken your portion and credited the buyer.

A lien on the property appears every January 1, and whoever owned it then stays liable. Where a lender escrows your taxes, the county recommends writing the loan number on a statement you receive and forwarding it to the lender.

Make sure your homestead status is recorded, since it shapes what the next owner pays. The school exemption is $140,000, and owners 65 and up or disabled get $60,000 more along with a school tax ceiling. Eligibility is the appraisal district's call, not the tax office's.

sections.h2: If the Conroe mortgage is behind
sections.html: Lenders usually wait until a loan is over 120 days late before sending a default notice with a 20 day cure period. Foreclosure sales happen on a first Tuesday, with the posted notice at least 21 days earlier. Finish a sale before that day and you decide the price. After an auction the lender may still pursue any shortfall for two years.

sections.h2: A tenant or an heir in the house
sections.html: A tenant generally receives three days' written notice, unless the lease says otherwise, and a disputed case lands in justice court. An occupant who never rented falls under property code chapter 24B and is removed through the sheriff or constable. Heirs need probate, a muniment of title, a small estate affidavit or a recorded transfer on death deed before a buyer will close.

sections.h2: How a Conroe cash sale works
sections.html:
Few steps are involved. Tell the buyer the address and the condition. An offer follows in writing, often after one visit. Accept it and the title company searches records, asks lenders for payoffs and books closing on your date. With no bank underwriting, only title work sets the pace.

Price is the cost. Cash offers deduct repairs and risk, whereas a listing can bring more after a longer wait. When the house is an estate, a rental or a loan near auction, speed can outweigh the gap.

sections.h2: Older core, lake homes and new subdivisions
sections.html:
Streets around the courthouse square hold houses from many decades. The courthouse itself dates to 1936, and downtown survived fires in 1901 and 1911. Lakeside homes and brand-new subdivisions sit in other price bands, so a buyer will want to know where your house fits.

Population climbed from 27,610 in 1990 to 43,617 in 2000 and an estimated 119,564 today. With that much building, many houses are fairly new, though roofs and systems differ in age. Write down when each major system was last replaced and hold on to the receipts.

sections.h2: Selling a Conroe rental with a tenant
sections.html:
A rental with a lease running can still sell, and some investors like it because rent keeps arriving. Hand over the lease, the ledger and the deposit amount, and state when the term ends. An investor will measure your rent against the local median of $1,393.

If the tenant has fallen behind, send the written notice before listing so the timeline is clear. The buyer will price in any delay, and tidy payment records make the house easier to value.

On the day, you sign the deed and the settlement statement. The title company pays off your mortgage and any back taxes first, divides the current year's bill with the buyer, then wires what is left. Bring photo identification and every key and garage remote. Arrange the final utility readings in advance, and leave the house empty unless the contract says otherwise.

Afterward the deed is filed with the county clerk. Keep a copy of the settlement statement with your own tax records, because it shows what portion of the year's bill you covered.

sections.h2: What to bring to the table
sections.html: Dig out the deed, your newest tax statement, each lender's payoff letter and any lease with its rent history. An inherited house adds probate papers to the pile. Ask every buyer who covers the title policy and how long the offer stays open. A brief list of known repairs heads off arguments.

faqs.a: Montgomery County. Its tax office is at 400 N. San Jacinto Street in Conroe and answers bill and payment questions.

faqs.q: What date do Conroe taxes turn delinquent?
faqs.a: February 1. The January 31 postmark deadline comes first, and after it a 6 percent penalty plus 1 percent interest begins.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Conroe house with taxes unpaid?
faqs.a: Yes. The balance is paid from your proceeds at closing, so ask for a tax certificate early to learn the amount.

faqs.q: Does Montgomery County take part payments?
faqs.a: Yes. Mark the check with the account number and the words partial payment. A balance still open after January 31 will draw penalty.

faqs.q: How soon before an auction must a lender send notice?
faqs.a: The notice must go out 21 or more days ahead of the first Tuesday sale, and only after the 20 day cure period on the default notice ends.
